## Function Assemble Batch

The requests of one generation → one OpenRouter batch submission, the whole batch inline as one JSON text.

Behaviour: assembleBatch(requests, config) is pure and returns a Batch Call. url = batchUrl(config.baseUrl), also exported: the baseUrl without trailing slashes, a final "/v1" replaced by "/beta", then "/batches"; a baseUrl not ending in /v1 keeps its path. headers as Assemble Request: Authorization "Bearer <apiKey>" (absent when apiKey is null), then Content-Type application/json. body is a JSON text, not an object (the provider stream-parses it and refuses requests before model), with exactly the keys endpoint "/v1/chat/completions", model = the config's model, requests, in this order. Each request becomes {custom_id, body} in request order; its body holds, in this order, max_tokens = the request's maxTokens (absent when null), reasoning = the request's or else the config's ({max_tokens: n} or {effort}; absent when both are null), messages as {role, content}. One model per batch: no item names a model (a request's own model is Send Batch's business); no provider, usage, tools, tool_choice or stream key.

Steps:
- reads: Request
- reads: Processor Config
- produces: Batch Call

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the config of the fixture; requests a.v1 {model: null, maxTokens: 12000, reasoning: null, messages: [{role: "user", content: "hi"}]} and a.v2 {model: null, maxTokens: null, reasoning: {effort: "low"}, messages: [{role: "system", content: "s"}, {role: "user", content: "u"}]}; when assembled; then url "https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches"; headers exactly {Authorization: "Bearer sk-or-test", Content-Type: "application/json"}; body is exactly {"endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"z-ai/glm-5.3:batch","requests":[{"custom_id":"a.v1","body":{"max_tokens":12000,"reasoning":{"max_tokens":2500},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}},{"custom_id":"a.v2","body":{"reasoning":{"effort":"low"},"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"s"},{"role":"user","content":"u"}]}}]} (ref: tests/fixtures/processor/batchConfig.json)
2. given the batch config with apiKey null, reasoning null and baseUrl "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1/"; request b.v1 {model: "x/y", maxTokens: null, reasoning: null, messages: [{role: "user", content: "hi"}]}; when assembled; then url "http://127.0.0.1:9/beta/batches"; headers exactly {Content-Type: "application/json"}; body is exactly {"endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","model":"z-ai/glm-5.3:batch","requests":[{"custom_id":"b.v1","body":{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}}]}; batchUrl("http://h/x/") is "http://h/x/batches"

Data Request: One provider-neutral chat request.

{
  "customId": "string — '<cardId>.v<n>'",
  "model": "string | null",
  "maxTokens": "number | null",
  "reasoning": "Card.reasoning",
  "messages": "{ role: 'system'|'user'|'assistant', content: string }[]"
}

Data Processor Config: One processor as read from the environment.
Schema:

Data Batch Call: One batch submission, ready to POST.
Schema:

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Read Batch

One reply about a batch (HTTP status + body text) into a Batch Read with the results mapped to Replies.

Behaviour: readBatch(status, text) is pure and never throws. Status outside 200..299 → state "error", error "http <status>: <error.message of the JSON body, else the first 200 chars of the text>"; a 2xx body that is not a JSON object → "unreadable response: <first 200 chars>"; one without a string status → "provider error: <error.message, else 'no batch status'>"; an error read has batchId null, status null, replies []. Otherwise batchId = id (null when not a string), status = the provider's word, state "done" for completed, "failed" for failed, expired, cancelled, canceled and cancelling, else "pending"; error = the batch's error.message (null when absent). replies: one per entry of results (none when results is not an array), in the provider's order, an entry without a string custom_id skipped. An entry with a non-null error → answer error "batch item error: <error.message, else the first 200 chars of its JSON>", text and finishReason null, usage 0 and 0 tokens, cost, provider and generationId null; an entry without a response object → "batch item error: no response", alike; otherwise Read Response of (custom_id, response.status_code, 200 when absent, the JSON text of response.body).

Steps:
- calls: Read Response
- produces: Batch Read

3. given status 200, the text of the fixture (a batch the provider rejected after accepting it); when read; then state "failed", status "failed", error "HTTP 400: invalid batch inference job: job-submission-count for account acct-0000, in use: 16, quota: 16", replies [] (ref: tests/fixtures/processor/batchFailed.json)
4. given status 404, the text of the fixture; when read; then exactly {batchId: null, state: "error", status: null, error: "http 404: Batch job batch-1789576284-Ejahe4wq9AgVdp5xGdNm not found.", replies: []} (ref: tests/fixtures/processor/batchNotFound.json)
5. given status 200, text "<html>bad gateway</html>"; when read; then state "error", error "unreadable response: <html>bad gateway</html>", batchId null, replies []

{ batchId: string | null, state: 'pending'|'done'|'failed'|'error', status: string | null, error: string | null, replies: { answer: Answer, usage: Usage }[] }

## Function Send Batch

One generation as one OpenRouter batch - submit once, poll until done or the wait runs out, map the results back to the requests.

Behaviour: sendBatch(config, requests, transport) never rejects; answers and usage come back in the order of requests, one each; exports BATCH_POLL_MS 15000 and BATCH_GRACE_MS 60000. A request whose model is set and differs from the config's is answered "batch runs one model: <customId> pins <model>, the batch is <config model>" and left out; no request left → no call. Submit: Assemble Batch of the rest, ONE transport.fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body}), never retried (a POST that reached the provider may already be a paid batch), then Read Batch: a thrown fetch → every request "batch submit: transport: <message>"; an error read → "batch submit: <its error>"; no batchId → "batch submit: no batch id". Poll: polls = max(1, floor(timeoutMs / BATCH_POLL_MS)), on this route TIMEOUT_MS is the whole wait; each poll sleeps transport.sleep(BATCH_POLL_MS) first, then transport.fetch(url + "/" + batchId, {method GET, headers}) with no body, then Read Batch. A thrown poll, status 408, 429 or 5xx, and a 404 while poll number × BATCH_POLL_MS ≤ BATCH_GRACE_MS (the provider's read-after-write lag) go on to the next poll; any other error read is final: every request "batch <batchId>: <its error>". pending → the next poll. done or failed → each request takes the first reply with its customId; a request without one → "batch <batchId> <status>: <the batch's error, else 'no result'>". Polls run out → every request "batch <batchId> still <the last status read, the submit's at first> after <polls> polls"; the batch is not cancelled. Every error answer has text and finishReason null, usage 0 and 0 tokens, cost, provider and generationId null.

Steps:
- calls: Assemble Batch
- calls: Read Batch
- produces: Answer
- produces: Usage

## Function Send Generation

Sends every Request of a generation, returns Answers and Usage per customId; retries transport errors with backoff; a provider refusal is recorded, not retried.

Behaviour: sendGeneration(config, requests, transport) never rejects; answers and usage come back in the order of requests, one each. Type stub → Stub Answer per request, no call, on either route. Type openrouter on route batch → Send Batch, its result as it is. Type openrouter on route sync: at most concurrency requests in flight; each is Assemble Request, then transport.fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body JSON}) and Read Response. A thrown fetch ("transport: <message>") or status 408, 429 or 5xx is retried up to maxRetries times, sleeping transport.sleep(1000 * 2^k) before retry k+1; any other status, refusals included, is final at once. A request still failing after retries gets " (after <attempts> attempts)" appended to its error.

Steps:
- calls: Assemble Request
- calls: Read Response
- calls: Stub Answer
- calls: Send Batch
- produces: Answer
- produces: Usage

Schema:

Callee Assemble Request: Request → provider JSON (OpenRouter chat completions) with provider.order + allow_fallbacks false when pinned, reasoning, usage.include; never tool_choice.
Behaviour: assembleRequest(request, config) is pure. url = baseUrl without trailing slashes + "/chat/completions"; headers Authorization "Bearer <apiKey>" (absent when apiKey is null) and Content-Type application/json. body: model = the request's model or the config's; messages copied as {role, content}; max_tokens = the request's maxTokens, absent when null; reasoning = the request's or else the config's, {maxTokens: n} as {max_tokens: n}, {effort} as is, absent when both are null; provider {order, allow_fallbacks: false} only when providerOrder is not null; usage {include: true} always. No other key: never tool_choice, tools or stream.

Callee Read Response: One provider reply (HTTP status + body text) into an Answer and its Usage.
Behaviour: readResponse(customId, status, text) is pure and never throws. Usage is read from any JSON body: id → generationId, provider, usage.prompt_tokens → inputTokens and usage.completion_tokens → outputTokens (0 when absent), usage.cost (null when absent). Status outside 200..299 → error "http <status>: <error.message of the JSON body, else the first 200 chars of the text>". Status 2xx: a body that is not JSON → "unreadable response: <first 200 chars>"; a body with an error object → "provider error: <error.message>"; no choices → "provider error: no choices"; otherwise text = choices[0].message.content (null when not a string: a reasoning model that spent its budget answers finish_reason "length" with no content, which is a truncation, not an error) and finishReason = choices[0].finish_reason.

Callee Stub Answer: The stub processor's answer to one Request, read from a directory of answer files; no network.
Behaviour: stubAnswer(request, config) reads <answersDir>/<customId>.md, else <answersDir>/<customId without its final .v<n>>.md; found → text = the file (UTF-8, as is), finishReason "stop", error null; usage 0 and 0 tokens, cost 0, provider "stub", generationId "stub-<customId>". Neither file → text null, finishReason null, error "stub has no answer: <answersDir>/<customId>.md".

Callee Send Batch: One generation as one OpenRouter batch - submit once, poll until done or the wait runs out, map the results back to the requests.
Behaviour: sendBatch(config, requests, transport) never rejects; answers and usage come back in the order of requests, one each; exports BATCH_POLL_MS 15000 and BATCH_GRACE_MS 60000. A request whose model is set and differs from the config's is answered "batch runs one model: <customId> pins <model>, the batch is <config model>" and left out; no request left → no call. Submit: Assemble Batch of the rest, ONE transport.fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body}), never retried (a POST that reached the provider may already be a paid batch), then Read Batch: a thrown fetch → every request "batch submit: transport: <message>"; an error read → "batch submit: <its error>"; no batchId → "batch submit: no batch id". Poll: polls = max(1, floor(timeoutMs / BATCH_POLL_MS)), on this route TIMEOUT_MS is the whole wait; each poll sleeps transport.sleep(BATCH_POLL_MS) first, then transport.fetch(url + "/" + batchId, {method GET, headers}) with no body, then Read Batch. A thrown poll, status 408, 429 or 5xx, and a 404 while poll number × BATCH_POLL_MS ≤ BATCH_GRACE_MS (the provider's read-after-write lag) go on to the next poll; any other error read is final: every request "batch <batchId>: <its error>". pending → the next poll. done or failed → each request takes the first reply with its customId; a request without one → "batch <batchId> <status>: <the batch's error, else 'no result'>". Polls run out → every request "batch <batchId> still <the last status read, the submit's at first> after <polls> polls"; the batch is not cancelled. Every error answer has text and finishReason null, usage 0 and 0 tokens, cost, provider and generationId null.
